<output>
# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)

# Let's try to understand cmatrix original code from memory.
# I recall cmatrix.c source exists, but we are not allowed to fetch it from internet.
# However we can reason from behavior.
# The executable is known to be cmatrix 2.0. Its behavior:
# - displays matrix rain.
# - options:
# We have established parsing rules:
# - usage goes to stdout, not stderr, exit 0, when missing arg for -u -C -t -M or unknown option or -h -?
# - invalid color goes to stderr with two lines " Invalid color selection\n Valid colors..."
#   Note leading space in our earlier output: " Invalid..."
#   Exactly: newline? We saw err starts with space.
#   Output: ' Invalid color selection\n Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.\n'
# - error opening tty: stderr "cmatrix: error: '<path>' couldn't be opened: <strerror>\n" exit 1
#   Also similar for opening terminal: "Error opening terminal: <term>.\n" exit 1 (no cmatrix: prefix)
#   And setfont/consolechars conflict: stderr " Unable to use both \"setfont\" and \"consolechars\".\n"
#   Note leading space.
#   What about exit code for that? We saw 0.
#   stdout for that case contains some curses init/cleanup sequence (like alternate screen).
# - version: stdout " CMatrix version 2.0 (compiled 23:10:28, Aug 10 2026)\nEmail: abishekvashok@gmail.com\nWeb: https://github.com/abishekvashok/cmatrix\n"
#   Leading space. Exit 0.
# - usage: stdout:
# " Usage: cmatrix -[abBcfhlsmVxk] [-u delay] [-C color] [-t tty] [-M message]\n"
# " -a: Asynchronous scroll\n"
# etc overall 19 lines? Let's check captured usage.txt earlier

PY
cat /tmp/h 2>/dev/null | od -c | head -n 100
python3 <<'PY'
import pathlib
data=pathlib.Path('/tmp/usage.txt').read_bytes() if pathlib.Path('/tmp/usage.txt').exists() else pathlib.Path('/tmp/h').read_bytes()
print(data.decode())
print("LEN",len(data))
# Show exact lines with leading spaces
for line in data.split(b'\n'):
    print(repr(line))

PY
"}

# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.
